automations.askText: When a new photo lands in {{folder}}, save a black-and-white copy of it in {{gray}}. Leave the original alone. Make it a command rule that uses file conversion (the grayscale preset of filee-cli). Turn on appendFiles so the new file paths arrive as command arguments, and exclude everything inside the black-and-white folder so the copies never trigger the rule again.

intro.title: Automations are made by talking
intro.body: There's no settings form. Tell the AI what you want and it builds the rule. Let's ask for: "when a photo lands in Downloads, make a black-and-white copy in a Black and White folder."

send.title: Press send
send.body: We wrote the request for you. Edit it if you like, or send it as it is.

asking.title: The AI is making the rule
asking.body: It's setting up a rule that watches the folder and saves black-and-white copies. If it asks for approval, allow it.

rule.title: The rule is ready
rule.body: A new rule appeared in your automations. One line shows the folder it watches, when it runs, and what it does. It keeps watching in the background even when the app is closed.

panes.title: Now let's see it work
panes.body: We'll split the window: Downloads on the left, a practice photos folder on the right. Move the photo to the left and watch.

drag.title: Drag the photo into Downloads
drag.body: Drag IMG_0001.jpg from the right into the Downloads folder on the left. Hold Option (Alt) while dragging to copy instead of move. The rule notices as soon as it lands.

result.title: A black-and-white photo appeared!
result.body: A black-and-white copy is now in the Black and White folder inside Downloads. From now on every photo that lands in Downloads gets one. This rule is just for practice, so feel free to delete it.

intro.title: Add your own button to the right-click menu
intro.body: Let's make an automation called "Peek at contents". Right-click a text file and it shows the size and first lines right away.

sample.title: Right-click the practice file
sample.body: We opened the Samples folder. Right-click the file and the button you just made shows up in the menu.

pick.title: There it is
pick.body: A right-click automation you make only appears when you right-click a matching file. Click it to run it.

result.title: The result is right there
result.body: The script read the size and first lines of the selected file. An AI automation that summarizes works the same way.

more.title: Make more of your own
more.body: In Settings › Right-click menu you can create automations by describing them, hide items, and reorder them. This example is for practice, so feel free to delete it.

offer.title: Want to try Remote Access?
offer.body: Open this computer's Dazzi from a browser on your phone or another computer. Nothing is opened until you switch it on yourself.

toggle.title: Turn it on and it's live
toggle.body: Turning it on starts a small web server on this computer. Nothing is opened until you switch it on yourself.

security.title: Trusted networks only
security.body: The connection is unencrypted HTTP. Keep it on only on a network you trust, like home or work, or through an encrypted tunnel.

connect.title: Devices pair with a code
connect.body: Once it's on, connection options appear below. Open the address on the new device and enter the pairing code shown here to register it. Registered devices can be renamed or removed in the list underneath.

fullDiskAccess.title: Full Disk Access needed
fullDiskAccess.leadTagColors: Finder's tag colors live in a location macOS protects. Turn Dazzi on in System Settings and choose Quit & Reopen when prompted.
fullDiskAccess.leadSource: This source reads another app's data. Turn on Full Disk Access for Dazzi in System Settings and choose Quit & Reopen when prompted.
fullDiskAccess.granted: Access is allowed. You're ready to continue.
